issues.problem: The opening presents acid as the necessary cause of curdling, with rennet only sometimes added. Rennet coagulation and acid coagulation are different routes, and rennet is an enzyme preparation rather than a single enzyme. This is a small factual overgeneralization. Manufacturer technical reference confirms acid, rennet, or combinations: https://dairyprocessinghandbook.tetrapak.com/chapter/cheese .
issues.suggested_replacement:
Most cheese starts with milk that is made to form curds. Depending on the cheese, acids, enzymes found in rennet, or both make milk proteins gather together. The watery liquid around the curds is called whey.

The curds are separated from the whey. Depending on the cheese, they may be cut, heated, salted, shaped, or pressed to remove more liquid. Some cheeses are eaten fresh. Others are aged, allowing enzymes and microbes to change their flavor and texture.

Different milk, cultures, and processing choices produce different cheeses.
issues.resolution: Applied suggested replacement before final dataset assembly.
